principal_reference.use: Principal appearance target; comparison only, no copied art or engine capability claim

comparison_regions.observation: The user found the Moore RPG scene hard to see and requested a scene from ProjectTitan. A complete Adventurer in its compatible source idle replaces the modular knight. The character is 1.8m tall, with unchanged proportions and original color/normal/packed PBR maps. The closer view is now the initial view; overview shows the larger surroundings. Judge readability in both actual captures; no human acceptance is claimed.

A market canopy/table, 0.85–0.9m barrels, 0.25–0.45m pottery/containers, 0.35–0.5m produce crates and a 0.5m stool surround the adventurer. The 4.8m house and 5.2m birch establish larger scale. Runtime bounds, exact declared heights and support placement are retained.

Grounded feet, barrel bases, the house and canopy meet a flat receiver textured with original Titan cobblestone PBR maps. The tabletop props use the measured table top as their support. Height/position, support contact, overhang and character-footprint checks reject incorrect placement. This is not AO/contact-depth effect feasibility.

Original Titan material colors, foliage, grassy roof and cobblestone supply the scene palette. Export-only PBR materials and unsaved conventional texture duplicates repair black/white conversion failures without changing source material samplers. Lighting is reduced to retain color. Final toon/outline choices remain T05.

proposed_bounds.bound: The 1.8m character must read clearly as a complete humanoid in the initial close view (4.5m ortho height) and remain identifiable in the overview (12m). Inspect head, torso, arms and separate boots at native 384×216; native-resolution images diagnose scene/asset quality but do not establish pixel readability.

Use physically sensible scene proportions: character 1.8m; small items 0.25–0.5m; barrels 0.85–0.9m; canopy 2.8m; house 4.8m; birch 5.2m. Pose precedes measurement; uniform scaling preserves proportions. Bases contact ground/support and the character footprint stays clear. Overview/close focus heights are 3.0m/1.0m.

The Adventurer silhouette remains separable from paving, the house and foliage in all three lighting states. Boots and building foundations meet the ground; architecture depth stays visible and amber light preserves character part separation.

T04/T09 must show no stationary pixel changes, no repeated crawl/shimmer on rigid edges during slow/diagonal tracking, no one-frame silhouette disappearance or outline-width pumping. One internal-pixel silhouette lines and selective convex highlights are reviewed in T05. No motion pass is claimed in T03.
No filled-surface outlines, stale reflection/depth frames, actor disappearance or unauthorized information in later combined cases; fallback deviations need explicit review.

proposed_deviations: User-selected Project Titan assets replace the Moore RPG fixture. A complete source Adventurer avoids modular-part alignment errors. The house, birch, market furniture and small props form a courtyard rather than an asset lineup.

The original ground receiver uses authored Titan cobblestone maps. The paving export supplies its material only. Uniform per-asset normalization establishes sensible comparison heights; these do not define gameplay dimensions.

Source graphs and virtual-texture readbacks produced black or white exports. Unsaved PBR materials and unsaved conventional texture duplicates transfer the original authored maps per slot, while preserving original material samplers. Export limitations remain explicit.

Reference-only framing uses orthographic height 12m for the whole courtyard and 4.5m for the initial closer view, with focus heights 3m/1m. T02 pixel resolution, presentation/window policy and angles remain unchanged. The character stays at normal height instead of being enlarged to compensate for distant framing.
No final toon/outline, motion, water, contact-depth, atmosphere or performance/package acceptance is claimed.

limitations: Eleven bounded exports supply a complete source character, nine scenery/prop meshes and a paving-material donor. Source and converted assets remain local.
Source cloth/wind/Blueprint/gameplay behavior is not transferred; the character is frozen in one compatible source idle.
Only selected PBR graphs/maps transfer. Unsaved texture duplicates disable virtual streaming for export without modifying original material samplers or saved input assets.
Paving geometry is an original flat receiver with tiled authored Titan cobblestone textures; terrain/steps do not authorize gameplay traversal.
